newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares seen steady after trade figures.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares seen steady after trade figures.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen steady early Thursday after digesting firmer-than-expected April non-oil exports and should attempt higher levels, dealers said.
"There might be some buying support for some stocks. They will be doing catch-up with those that firmed recently," a dealer with a local broking house.
With April non-oil exports up 5.9 percent, compared with a Reuters' average forecast of a 0.5 percent rise, institutional demand was seen for smaller capitalisation stocks.
On Tuesday, the Straits Times Industrials Index closed up 3.05 points at 2,053.99 after touching a high of 2,072.07.
Technical analysts said the market has to break 2,118 on the upside to resume its uptrend.
The market was closed on Wednesday for a public holiday.
